response.sql: WITH rc AS (SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.City, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City), ca AS (SELECT EmployeeId, City, cnt, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER (PARTITION BY City) AS city_avg FROM rc), kept AS (SELECT EmployeeId, City, cnt, city_avg, SUM(cnt) OVER () AS total_kept FROM ca WHERE cnt > city_avg) SELECT City, SUM(cnt) AS total_customers, AVG(cnt - city_avg) AS avg_excess_over_city_avg, AVG(cnt * 1.0 / total_kept) AS avg_share FROM kept GROUP BY City

assumptions.assumption: Reps are grouped by EmployeeId and city; the city average is taken over reps in that city who have at least one matched customer (reps with zero customers do not appear).
The share denominator is the total customer count of all kept above-average reps across all cities, and shares use non-integer division. A city with NULL City is treated as its own group.
